done_when: When forge work continues an item's existing Codex conversation, the prompt carries only the round's summary line, the coordinator's note or answer, the open findings and failing checks, one line saying the earlier brief still applies, and the changes since the last turn ended (not since it started); a first turn or a fresh conversation still gets the full brief; tests through forge work show both

findings.body: The saved `head` is only a commit SHA (`src/forge/codex.py:345`), so it does not capture uncommitted files present when the turn ended. If those files remain unchanged through another round, `_changes` sends them again as new changes. This occurs in the existing CLI scenario: `tests/test_codex_resume.py:245` expects the third turn to receive uncommitted files already sent to the second turn. Preserve an end-of-turn working-tree baseline so subsequent prompts include only intervening changes. This is P2 advice for the dirty-checkout edge case; the ordinary committed-worker case is fixed.
findings.title: Exclude already-seen uncommitted edits from continuation diffs

why: Every fix round resends the whole worker brief into the same Codex conversation, and its 'since your last turn' diff includes the worker's own changes
